The current arrow is drawn on the left/front side of the loop and goes upward along the loop. A bar magnet is located above the current loop, with the left end labeled N and the right end labeled S. Reasoning: Use the right-hand rule for the current loop located in the y-z plane; when the current is upward on the +z/front side, the magnetic dipole moment of the current loop points toward -x. A north magnetic pole in an external magnetic field is acted on by a force in the direction of the magnetic field, so the force on the north pole points toward +x.

raw_record.question_text: A long bar magnet is placed above a current loop oriented as shown. In which direction will the North pole of the bar magnet feel a force due to the current loop?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the loop is drawn in the y-z plane, with +y upward, +x to the right, and the current arrow on the left/front side of the loop pointing upward. The bar magnet is above the top of the loop, with its N pole on the left side of the magnet and S pole on the right. Use the current direction and the right-hand rule to determine the loop’s magnetic dipole moment: with current upward on the +z/front side of a y-z loop, the loop’s dipole moment points in the -x direction. The North pole of the magnet is above the loop, i.e. in the equatorial region of this current-loop dipole, where the magnetic field points opposite the dipole moment. Therefore the field at the North pole points in the +x direction. Since a North magnetic pole feels force in the direction of the external magnetic field, the force is +x.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中电流环是一个竖直椭圆，位于 y-z 平面内；坐标轴显示 +y 向上，+x 向右，+z 斜向左下。电流箭头画在环的左侧/前侧，并沿环向上。长条形磁铁位于电流环上方，左端标为 N，右端标为 S。推理：对位于 y-z 平面的电流环使用右手定则；在 +z/front 一侧电流向上时，电流环的磁偶极矩指向 -x。磁铁的北极位于环上方，属于该电流环磁偶极子的赤道区域；在赤道区域，磁场方向与磁偶极矩相反，因此此处磁场指向 +x。北磁极在外磁场中受力方向沿磁场方向，所以北极受到的力指向 +x。
method.answer_match_reason: The predicted answer '+x' exactly matches the standard answer '+x'.

answer_match_part_results.reason: Both indicate the force on the North pole is in the positive x direction.
